payload.claim: `_resolve_stacked_on`'s docstring says the parent's task is chosen as 'the newest row in a `scheduler.DEPENDENCY_WAITING_STATES` state ... the same waiting-outranks-dead precedence `scheduler._dependency_refusal` gives it' (line 180-182), i.e. an older waiting row is preferred over a newer dead one. That is only true when `gh` is `None`. When a `GhRunner` is passed (the default from `saffron cell` after this change, per `cli.py`'s new `gh=_guarded_gh(...)` argument), the function instead takes the absolute newest task row regardless of state (`newest_task = rows[-1]`, line 235) and explicitly refuses to fall back to an older waiting row if that newest row is dead. The docstring was not updated to describe this second, now-default-for-attended-runs selection rule, so it misdescribes the function's actual contract for its primary caller.
